variants.headline: The treasury slips into deficit
body: The treasury now takes in {{deficit}} gold less than it spends each turn. A sailmaker who fills orders from the {{terms.civic.government}} says he is cutting only as much canvas as the first installment will cover.

variants.headline: The books, newly behind
body: Last count: the books at balance or better.
This count: the books behind.
Behind by: {{deficit}} gold, every season.

variants.headline: A bill that comes back every season
body: The treasury is spending {{deficit}} gold a season more than it takes in. Sell a piece of public land and the proceeds might cover this season's bill. At the current rate, the same bill comes due next season, with one piece of land fewer to sell. Any minister who proposes a sale should bring next season's figures too.

variants.headline: Sir, the treasury now outspends its income
body: I keep a stall by the east gate. When I spend more than I take, my wife hears of it before the market closes, and the week after there is no honey on the table. The treasury now spends {{deficit}} gold a season more than it takes. Who in the {{terms.civic.government}} hears of it, and what goes missing from their table?

variants.headline: The treasury passes a thousand gold
body: A supplier waiting at the public pay window this morning asked how much of the thousand gold was already spoken for. The treasury has crossed the mark at {{gold}} gold, up {{gain}} since the last count.

variants.headline: The reserve reaches the thousand mark
body: The treasury has reached the thousand mark and holds {{gold}} gold, up {{gain}} from the last count. Among the capital's old families, the question is whether the vault's new weight will reach the notes they hold before the winter.

variants.headline: Hear it! A thousand gold in the vault!
body: Hear it, {{terms.civic.people}}, hear it! The treasury has passed the thousand-gold mark and holds {{gold}} gold in the vault. A thousand gold and more, counted and kept, counted and kept!

variants.headline: The treasury just crossed 1,000 gold
body: Reserve: {{gold}} gold. Up {{gain}} gold over the last few seasons. The thousand mark is behind us, and the number is exact.

variants.headline: The treasury gains time against the deficit
body: The plasterer who waits by the treasury door each reckoning says he can hand in his account this time. The treasury holds {{gold}} gold against a shortfall of {{deficit}} a turn, enough for {{turnsLeft}} full turns at the current rate.

variants.headline: What the treasury can do with more time
body: At a shortfall of {{deficit}} gold a season, the treasury now has enough in reserve for {{turnsLeft}} full seasons. At the tax office, a collector with a list of overdue accounts has time to knock on doors before the notices go up. If the list comes good, the {{terms.civic.government}} may get through the season without reaching for a new tax. The advantage lasts only while receipts and spending hold near today's figures.

variants.headline: The count runs long at the money-changer's table
body: Not long ago, the money-changers were counting the treasury's remaining seasons on their fingers, and nobody liked the total. This morning the tally at the table ran to {{turnsLeft}} seasons of cover, {{gold}} gold against {{deficit}} a season, and the talk over the coins came easier. The oldest of them still kept his coat on. Habits.

variants.headline: The treasury reserve runs short
body: At the gate, a carter hauling stone for the walls has begun asking for his fee when the load is tipped rather than at the month's end. The clerk paid him from the chest by the door. The treasury holds {{gold}} gold against a deficit of {{deficit}} a season, enough to cover {{turnsLeft}} more seasons at the present rate.

variants.headline: The treasury, counted
body: The vault holds: {{gold}} gold.
The court spends beyond its income: {{deficit}} gold a season.
At this rate the vault answers for {{turnsLeft}} seasons, and no more.

variants.headline: Treasury cover: {{turnsLeft}} full turns left
body: A woman who brings grain to the public stores has one question for the {{terms.civic.government}}: who gets paid first if the money runs out? The treasury holds {{gold}} gold tonight, and with spending ahead of revenue by {{deficit}} gold a turn, that is {{turnsLeft}} full turns of cover at the current rate.

variants.headline: The old rule was a full store
body: Councilors, the treasury holds {{gold}} gold and loses {{deficit}} a turn, which leaves {{turnsLeft}} full turns at this rate. Put next week's pay and grain bills on the table before you vote another expense; the people who fill our stores will soon need to know which orders they can afford to take.

variants.headline: The deficit ends
body: In the yard where the barrels are made, a woman who has been taking public orders a barrel at a time says she will ask whether she can deliver the rest at once. The treasury is out of deficit, with {{goldPerTurn}} gold to spare each turn at the latest count.

variants.headline: The state pays its way
body: The treasury now clears {{goldPerTurn}} gold a season, after a count that showed a shortfall. On the riverfront, a shipwright who had been taking payment in installments has taken a contract for a second hull and hired two more hands. The yard has work into the next season.

variants.headline: Notice: the accounts no longer run behind
body: Notice is given that the treasury no longer spends more than it takes in, with {{goldPerTurn}} gold now left over each turn. Merchants with unpaid accounts may bring their receipts when the pay office opens.

variants.headline: The purse that stopped leaking
body: They say a stopped leak is the first gold in the purse. The treasury's leak has stopped.

variants.headline: Hear it! The lean stretch is over!
body: Hear it, {{terms.civic.people}}, hear it! Income now beats spending by {{goldPerTurn}} gold a season, and the deficit is done with! The lean stretch is behind us, behind us!
